newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent gains eroded by bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent gains eroded by bearish sentiment.

text.p: IPE Brent crude prices saw some of the day's gains eroded on Thursday afternoon as the previous day's bears re-appeared, brokers said.
There was very little fundamental news, but dealers said reports of limited progress in the Iraqi oil sales deal with the United Nations helped the negative sentiment.
January Brent stood 33 cents up on the day at $22.87 per barrel at 1854 GMT. Earlier, Dec gas oil closed $4.75 lower at $219.00 per tonne, catching up with crude's $1.00 per barrel drop on Wednesday.
"Brent is 20 cents off the high and looking vulnerable," a broker said, pegging support at $22.68 and $22.38.
A Western diplomat at the United Nations in New York said on Wednesday that if current U.N.-sponsored inspector visits to Iraq went well, the oil sales deal could be implemented in February 1997.

Gas oil prices dropped sharply on Thursday to reflect crude's near-$1.00 per barrel drop the night before, but its relative value to crude also fell. January Brent/gas oil closed at $6.25 per barrel, from $7.00 on Wednesday.
"The gas oil was sold heavily into the close, but there was no real crack activity pushing it down," a broker said.
